# Single-matrix Pfaffian

## Decisions

- Partial pivoted Parlett–Reid reduction follows Wimmer, *Algorithm 923*
  (ACM TOMS 38(4), 2012; arXiv:1102.3440, §II.B and Appendix B).
  Only every other column needs elimination for the Pfaffian. Stored multiplier
  pairs accumulate `X Yᵀ − Y Xᵀ`; transposes do not conjugate complex inputs.
- Satyarth et al., arXiv:2411.09859v2, §§3.6–3.7, explains the ordered pivoted
  panel and parallel trailing update. This implementation chooses a 32-column
  panel. That choice remains provisional: the diagnostic scaling target is not
  met. Pivot selection, pending-column updates, permutations and normalization
  remain serial.
- Each completed panel partitions the strict lower triangle into equal-area,
  contiguous column ranges with the existing `lower_area_split`. The existing
  derived cost gate, using the Bunch–Kaufman rate as a provisional proxy, chooses
  the active width. The caller-held Team runs those ranges through `team::run`;
  Seq runs the same block kernel with one participant. There is no new executor.
- Native SIMD uses the existing pulp runtime dispatch. Pivot ties choose the
  smallest row. Rank-two updates batch four independent vectors with the existing
  `batch_indices` helper, retaining masked/remainder coverage and per-entry FMA
  order. The rank-two sum order and final product tree do not depend on team
  width or vector lanes; ordinary fused arithmetic can still differ across ISAs.
  A completed gpt-6.1-sol delta review found no defects; the final 60 native
  benchmark cases agree bitwise with e513063. This is not a speedup proof.
- The immutable-input API takes `MemStack` with a `pfaffian_scratch` query,
  rather than the issue's allocating two-argument sketch. This honors #111's
  no-per-call-allocation rule without adding an allocating wrapper or TLS cache.
  The strict lower triangle is authoritative; skew symmetry is a caller
  precondition, like adjacent symmetric factorizations. Zero pivots and
  nonfinite/underflowed results are errors. Scaled/log Pfaffians, inverse and
  batched APIs are outside this change.
- Numerical code was derived from published equations, not copied or translated
  from PfaPack, mvmc-rs, or xrq-phys/Pfapack. Only the latter repository's README,
  filenames and LAPACK license file were consulted for structure; this makes no
  claim that that license covers every file. No reference numerical source was
  imported; the tests use independently written recursive/congruence oracles.

## Verification conclusions and constraints

- Ten focused tests pass with both default features and `x86-v4`:
  f32/f64/c32/c64 recursive definitions through n=8 and determinant identities;
  known-Pfaffian congruences and forced nonadjacent swaps across panel boundaries;
  pivot ties and masked tails; invalid shape, singularity, nonfinite arithmetic,
  underflow and normal/subnormal scale cases; strided input with ignored NaN upper
  entries; input preservation; and scratch shortage. Extended-precision real and
  complex cases also pass. Oracle comparisons explicitly reject nonfinite
  operands rather than accepting an infinite relative-error bound.
- Seq and Team budgets 1/3/8/32 agree exactly on n=258 fixtures for all four
  native scalar types; dispatch counters verify real multi-participant column
  sections, not just a Team token.
  The existing process-wide allocation guard reports zero allocations during
  complete held-team Pfaffian calls (budgets 4/8/70), and verifies dispatch;
  it passes in default and `x86-v4` configurations.
- Three new doctests and the std-only build pass. No-std checks pass both with
  no default features and explicitly with `--no-default-features --features
  linalg`; the latter reports 28 warnings outside the Pfaffian delta.
  Scoped nightly rustfmt checks of the new module/test pass. Repository-wide
  nightly `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails in existing unrelated source;
  no mass formatting changes are retained. Repository-wide Clippy remains
  blocked by deny-lint errors in unchanged code (the traits' `eq_op`, then old
  factorization SIMD index expansions with `--no-deps`); no suppressions or
  unrelated fixes were added. Rustdoc builds, with four existing unresolved
  links: `ParShape::dispatch_cost`, `run`, `fork`, `for_each_child`.
  The inherited library suite with `--features unstable` passes on the final
  numerical source: 588 passed, 138 ignored, zero failed. Ignored tests were
  not executed.
- Both tested configurations actually select `pulp::x86::v3::V3`: four f64 or two
  c64 values per SIMD vector on this EPYC 7702P. There is no AVX-512 execution
  evidence. The existing manifest unconditionally enables `pulp/x86-v3`; a
  scalar-only Cargo build is not exposed. No feature defaults were changed.
- The approved broccoli diagnostic attempted 90 cells: 84 guard-accepted and six
  missing; both original performance gates remain unmet. This is not performance
  adoption: no unchanged upstream control was timed. The full table, raw samples,
  reference identities and refusal records follow. Team32 performance and actual
  AVX-512 execution remain unperformed, tracked by #173 rather than claimed by
  the 32-thread correctness tests above.

## Four-way diagnostic: performance gates NOT met

This is a maintainer-approved shared-host diagnostic, **not** a paired v2
adoption campaign: no unchanged upstream control was timed. All 90 declared
cells were attempted once at the final numerical revision; **84 accepted,
6 idle-rejected and missing**, not silently retried. A missing cell is not zero,
a skipped implementation, or a passing gate. No push/PR/CI/auto-merge has been
performed for this checkpoint; the performance acceptance remains unresolved.

### Identity and protocol

- Numerical revision: `96c32abb945d3cb856005aff8501d2132ba6c886`;
  `faer/src/linalg/pfaffian/mod.rs` SHA-256
  `10dc90e15bdbf84773eaff1f86404add75ffb3839ea9c96ed7778d33f5b7721b`.
  Only documentation was dirty during timing. Raw receipts, executable/lockfile
  hashes, scripts and references remain in `/home/shinaoka/work/pfaffian-ref/`:
  `environment-batch4.json`, `grid-batch4.json`,
  `measure-batch4/{complete.json,raw.jsonl,*.guard.log,*.stdout}`.
  No comparison harness is added to faer; a reusable harness needs a separate
  faer-benchmark PR.
- Host: broccoli, AMD EPYC 7702P, AVX2 exposed and no AVX-512. Runtime topology
  reports four cores per L3 domain. Measured CPUs: **1T=4, Team4=4-7,
  Team8=4-11**. Team8 spans two L3 domains under explicit maintainer permission.
  Observer and all identified own observer descendants: **0-3,36-63**.
  Other people's processes were not stopped or moved. Team32 performance on evo
  and actual AVX-512 execution remain unperformed: [#173](https://github.com/tensor4all/faer/issues/173).
- Fixed common seed171, uniform[-2,2]/sqrt(n), independent complex components;
  headerless little-endian column-major f64 or interleaved c64. Every arm reads
  the exact same file for a cell. n2 has an analytic smoke fixture; n64/128/256/
  512/1024 are the timed grid. All 90 untimed reference/candidate cases passed
  relative comparison at 5e-9 before timing. All 60 final faer cases additionally
  agree bitwise with e513063 (untimed, including both builds and all budgets).
- **Three warmups, ten steady-clock samples, median**, one case at a time.
  Working buffers/workspace and held Teams are created outside timing where the
  API permits; every timer includes the matrix-reset copy, or faer's internal
  immutable-input copy. Public API internal allocations not removable by the
  runner are included, not subtracted. Input parsing/startup is excluded.
- `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`, Julia one thread.
  BLAS/Julia thread counts are checked at runtime. No target-cpu=native flags.
  Before each case the coordinator checks competing builds/measurements and
  holds the existing campaign lock. Existing `pinned.sh` checks pre/post idle:
  3s window, max busy0.05, one attempt (`PINNED_RETRIES=1`). Builds completed
  before timing. Long commands use `supervise.sh` with bounded stall/max time.

The crates.io pfapack0.2.0 Fortran wrapper is **not** the mvmc baseline and is
not counted in the four-way table. An initially selected tmisawa/PfaPack.jl
snapshot is not counted either. The actual Julia-mVMC pinned package's
`pfaffian_ltl!` convenience route passed n2 but failed the common n64/c64 check;
its results/timings were not accepted. The named public full-LTL-plus-product
route passed all grid sizes. This is an API-specific comparison, not a claim
about the fastest possible Julia or opt-in mvmc configuration. No mvmc or
crates.io numerical implementation body was read/copied for faer's code.

### Gate assessment

Thresholds were **not weakened**: Seq/Fortran <=1.05 at every reported cell,
Team8 >=4x the fastest single-thread median at n>=256. The fastest single
includes both faer builds and all three reference implementations, not just
Fortran. When a single-thread cell is missing, the known-minimum speedup is an
**upper bound**, not proof of passing.

| n | dtype | default Seq/Fortran | v4 Seq/Fortran | default best1T/Team8 | v4 best1T/Team8 |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | f64 | 1.180 | 1.158 | 0.852 | 0.856 |
| 64 | c64 | N/A | 0.715 | <=0.887 | <=0.892 |
| 128 | f64 | 0.883 | 0.896 | N/A | 0.925 |
| 128 | c64 | 0.614 | 0.609 | 1.301 | 1.314 |
| 256 | f64 | 0.891 | 0.828 | 1.324 | 1.430 |
| 256 | c64 | 0.756 | 0.749 | 1.721 | 1.720 |
| 512 | f64 | 1.026 | 1.025 | 2.020 | 2.057 |
| 512 | c64 | N/A | 0.666 | <=2.540 | N/A |
| 1024 | f64 | 1.052 | 1.054 | 2.739 | 2.803 |
| 1024 | c64 | 0.596 | 0.594 | 3.572 | 3.604 |

Seq fails for f64/n64 (1.158-1.180x) and f64/n1024 (1.052-1.054x).
All evaluable n>=256 Team8 speedups are below4; the largest measured value is
3.604x at c64/n1024. The six missing cells prevent an all-cells pass as well.
Actual multi-participant dispatch and zero allocation establish correctness of
the Team path, not its scaling target; that path is retained. Ordered pivot
search, pending-panel updates, permutations and normalization remain serial;
32-column blocking and the borrowed Bunch-Kaufman cost proxy are still
provisional. No phase-level timing establishes which serial/cache/dispatch
component dominates. Hardware profiling was not run: `perf` is unavailable on PATH;
no profiling infrastructure was installed to work around that.

The four-vector change was motivated by the e513063 n64/f64 diagnostic,
where the original 5% target already failed. The final values below are
separate, unpaired measurements and do **not** establish a gated before/after
speedup.
Earlier `measure-grid` (own observer descendants were not all pinned),
`measure-observer-fixed`, and two foreign-build-aborted remaining-grid runs
are preserved separately; none is pooled into these final medians. Foreign
workspace/default/parallel build conflicts stopped those runs before their
first remaining numeric case. A redesign or a waiver of the original
performance acceptance is not silently adopted; no PR is opened on this basis.
